sQK3Yr4Sc_k.title: Photosynthesis: Crash Course Biology #8
sQK3Yr4Sc_k.note: 13744 characters. Added so conclusions are not drawn from one video. Deliberately as far from programming as possible: no shared vocabulary, which is what makes the cross-video case meaningful.

notes: Every expect_chunk_containing substring was verified to appear in EXACTLY ONE chunk at chunk sizes 450, 600, 900 and 1200. test_retrieval_eval_fixture.py re-checks this on every run, offline. Seven earlier candidates were rejected by that check - 'try and accept' and 'hey there' look distinctive to a human but land in two chunks, and 'convert mario' is unique at 450/900/1200 yet duplicated at 600 by the overlap segment. Do not add a case without running the check.

search_query is the FROZEN rewrite: what _contextualize produced for that case, recorded so a measurement can hold it constant. The rewrite calls a chat model and is not deterministic; leaving it live made the 5-case predecessor swing by a whole case between runs, which was larger than the effect any chunk-size comparison was trying to measure. Runners use it in frozen mode and ignore it in live mode.

off_topic cases assert the OPPOSITE of a hit: nothing in the video should match well. Without them a case set cannot detect a system that returns confident garbage, because every other case rewards returning something. The 0.78 threshold is measured, not guessed - on-topic questions score 0.48-0.66 and off-topic ones 0.87-0.94 at chunk size 600.

The off_topic threshold was re-measured on the second video rather than assumed to carry over. Biology on-topic questions score 0.39-0.53 and off-topic ones 0.85-0.93, so 0.78 separates both videos with margin.

cases.name: first turn, arithmetic
cases.question: How do I do addition in Python?
cases.search_query: How do I do addition in Python?
cases.guards: A first turn must be searched with the raw question - there is no history to resolve against, so a rewrite could only make a good query worse.

cases.name: first turn, while loop
cases.question: How does a while loop work?
cases.search_query: How does a while loop work?
cases.guards: Same as first-addition.

cases.name: first turn, tooling
cases.question: What code editor does the tutorial use?
cases.search_query: What code editor does the tutorial use?
cases.guards: The standalone form of followup-it-uses. If this hits and followup-it-uses misses, the rewrite is the problem, not retrieval.

cases.name: first turn, exponentiation
cases.question: How do I raise a number to a power in Python?
cases.search_query: How do I raise a number to a power in Python?
cases.guards: Vocabulary mismatch: the transcript never says 'raise to a power', only 'exponential power' and 'two asterisks'.

cases.name: first turn, lists
cases.question: How do I create a list?
cases.search_query: How do I create a list?
cases.guards: The weakest on-topic question measured (0.6644 at size 600). Kept deliberately as the case most likely to break first.

cases.name: first turn, pass keyword
cases.question: What is the pass keyword for?
cases.search_query: What is the pass keyword for?
cases.guards: The expected chunk is the one explaining WHY pass exists, not the one introducing it.

cases.name: follow-up referring to the previous answer

history.content: What is this video about?
This video is about getting started with Python in less than 10 minutes.

cases.question: And what did you just say it uses?
cases.search_query: What did you just say the video uses to get started with Python?
cases.guards: The originally observed failure. Without the rewrite this carries no information about the video and returns arbitrary neighbours.

cases.name: follow-up asking for an example

history.content: What does the pass keyword do?
pass lets you define a function without writing its logic yet.

cases.question: give me an example of one
cases.search_query: give me an example of the pass keyword in a function definition
cases.guards: 'one' resolves to a function stub, which only the history can supply.

cases.name: follow-up asking how to exit

history.content: What is an infinite loop?
It is a while true loop whose condition never becomes false.

cases.question: and how do I make it stop?
cases.search_query: how do I make an infinite loop stop?
cases.guards: 'it' is the loop from the previous turn.

cases.name: follow-up about variable naming

history.content: How do I assign a value to a variable?
Pick a name such as item and assign it a value, for example a string.

cases.question: is it case sensitive?
cases.search_query: Is variable assignment case sensitive?
cases.guards: Answerable only if 'it' resolves to variable names.

cases.name: follow-up about a condition never ending

history.content: How does a while loop work?
It increments i by one until i reaches five, then exits.

cases.question: what if the condition is never false?
cases.search_query: what happens if the condition in a while loop is never false?
cases.guards: Carries real content already, so the rewrite must not make it worse - the failure mode this case watches is over-rewriting.

cases.name: vague follow-up, next topic

history.content: How does a while loop work?
It increments i by one until i reaches five.

cases.question: and the next one?
cases.search_query: How does a while loop work?
cases.guards: The hallucination guard. The conversation never says what comes next in the video, so the rewrite must NOT invent a topic. Measured behaviour so far: the model restates the previous question instead of advancing - it does not hallucinate, but it also does not resolve the reference, and the case has passed on chunk adjacency rather than on capability. Read its rewrite, not only its verdict.

cases.name: vague follow-up, other branches

history.content: How do if statements work?
If the age is more than 21 the program prints that you are old.

cases.question: what about the other branches?
cases.search_query: what about the other branches of if statements?
cases.guards: 'other branches' is resolvable from the history - unlike vague-next, a correct rewrite is genuinely possible here.

cases.name: vague follow-up, another instance

history.content: Why would I write a function?
To reuse code - the greeting function is called once with mario.

cases.question: show me another one
cases.search_query: show me another reason to write a function
cases.guards: 'another one' means a second call, not a second function. A rewrite that reads it as 'another function' will land elsewhere.

cases.name: topic shift away from the history

history.content: How does a for loop work?
for i in range of three loops over three values and prints hello with i.

cases.question: actually, how do I handle errors?
cases.search_query: How do I handle errors?
cases.guards: The opposite failure of followup-it-uses: the question is already self-contained and has NOTHING to do with the history. A rewrite that drags loops into it will retrieve the wrong passage. No earlier case tested this direction.

cases.name: explicit topic abandonment

history.content: How do I multiply two numbers?
You add an asterisk between the two values.

cases.question: forget that - what are quotation marks for?
cases.search_query: What are quotation marks for?
cases.guards: States the abandonment outright. If even this gets anchored to the prior topic, the rewrite prompt weights history too heavily.

cases.name: off-topic, database connection
cases.question: How do I connect to a PostgreSQL database?
cases.search_query: How do I connect to a PostgreSQL database?
cases.guards: Nothing in the video answers this. Every other case rewards returning something, so without a case like this the set cannot detect a system that answers confidently from irrelevant chunks.

cases.name: off-topic, infrastructure

history.content: How does a while loop work?
It increments i by one until i reaches five.

cases.question: How do I configure Kubernetes ingress with TLS?
cases.search_query: How do I configure Kubernetes ingress with TLS?
cases.guards: Off-topic WITH history, so it also checks that the rewrite does not manufacture a false connection to the conversation just because history exists.

cases.name: first turn, vascular plants
cases.question: What is a vascular plant?
cases.search_query: What is a vascular plant?
cases.guards: Second video, same guard as first-addition: no history means no rewrite.

cases.name: first turn, ATP production
cases.question: How does the plant make ATP?
cases.search_query: How does the plant make ATP?
cases.guards: The expected chunk is the ATP Synthase mechanism, not the later mentions of ATP as a currency.

cases.name: first turn, naming of the dark reactions
cases.question: Why are the dark reactions badly named?
cases.search_query: Why are the dark reactions badly named?
cases.guards: Vocabulary mismatch of the second video: the transcript argues the name is a 'misnomer', never 'badly named'.

cases.name: first turn, photosystem II composition
cases.question: How many chemicals are in photosystem II?
cases.search_query: How many chemicals are in photosystem II?
cases.guards: A numeric fact, which embeddings handle poorly - the case most likely to fail on a weaker embedding model.

cases.name: follow-up asking for the full name

history.content: What is photosystem II?
It is the first of four protein complexes in the light-dependent reactions.

cases.question: what is its full name?
cases.search_query: What is the full name of photosystem II?
cases.guards: 'its' is only resolvable from the history, and the answer is a term no one would search for directly.

cases.name: follow-up about handling a byproduct

history.content: What does RuBisCo get wrong?
About half the time it grabs oxygen instead of CO2, creating a toxic byproduct.

cases.question: what do plants do with it?
cases.search_query: What do plants do with the toxic byproduct created when RuBisCo grabs oxygen instead of CO2?
cases.guards: 'it' is the byproduct from the previous turn.

cases.name: follow-up asking for the analogy

history.content: Why do plants pump protons into the thylakoid?
To build a concentration gradient across the membrane.

cases.question: what is that like?
cases.search_query: What is it like for plants to pump protons into the thylakoid to build a concentration gradient across the membrane?
cases.guards: Asks for an analogy the transcript actually makes. A rewrite that turns this into a mechanism question will miss it.

cases.name: vague follow-up, what comes first

history.content: What are the light-dependent reactions?
They are stage one of photosynthesis, and they happen in the thylakoid membrane.

cases.question: and what happens first?
cases.search_query: What happens first in the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis?
cases.guards: Second video's counterpart to vague-next: a vague follow-up whose reference the history CAN resolve. Retargeted on 2026-08-07 after it failed at every chunk size except 1200. The failure was not over-specification, as first suspected, but UNDER-ANCHORING: the earlier history said only that photosynthesis has two kinds of reactions, so 'first' could mean either the first stage or the first event within it. The rewrite chose the former and retrieval correctly returned the overview passage at rank 1 - the fixture was demanding worse behaviour than the system produced. The history now names the light-dependent reactions, so 'first' resolves to the first event inside them, and photoexcitation is reachable at rank 2. Keep the question vague; anchoring belongs in the history, which is what this case kind exists to test.

cases.name: vague follow-up, name of the step

history.content: What starts the Calvin cycle?
A CO2 molecule gets attached to RuBP.

cases.question: what's that called?
cases.search_query: What is the process called when a CO2 molecule gets attached to RuBP to start the Calvin cycle?
cases.guards: 'that' is the step described in the previous answer.

cases.name: topic shift to respiration

history.content: What happens in the reduction phase?
ATP and NADPH convert 3-Phosphoglycerate into G3P.

cases.question: forget the cycle - how does photosynthesis relate to respiration?
cases.search_query: How does photosynthesis relate to respiration?
cases.guards: Explicit abandonment, second video. The expected passage is at the very start, far from the history's topic.

cases.name: cross-video: a question the OTHER video answers
cases.question: How do I write a for loop in Python?
cases.search_query: How do I write a for loop in Python?
cases.guards: Only possible with two videos in the set: this question is answered in detail by fWjsdhR3z3c, but is scoped to sQK3Yr4Sc_k. It checks that the video_id filter really scopes the search and that no accidental vocabulary bridge exists. Measured at 0.9260 against the biology chunks - far above the threshold.
